extra.message: User-controlled input from get_argument('username') and get_argument('password') is concatenated directly into a SQL query string passed to cur.execute(). An attacker can inject SQL (e.g. username = admin'--) to bypass authentication or extract data. Use parameterized queries instead.

User-controlled input from get_argument('server') is concatenated into a shell command passed to os.popen('ping -c 3 ' + server). An attacker can inject arbitrary OS commands (e.g. server = '127.0.0.1; cat /etc/passwd') leading to remote code execution.

User-controlled input from get_argument('file') is concatenated into a file path ('read/' + file_name) and opened for reading without sanitization. An attacker can use path traversal sequences (e.g. file=../../../../etc/passwd) to read arbitrary files on the server.

The StaticHandler builds a file path by concatenating the user-controlled URL path segment ('static/' + path) and opens it without sanitization. An attacker can use path traversal sequences (e.g. /static/../../etc/passwd) to read arbitrary files outside the static directory.

The 'query' and 'link' values originate from the user-controlled get_argument('q') in SearchHandler and are rendered with Tornado's {% raw %} directive, which disables HTML autoescaping. The 'link' value is also injected inside a <script> string context. This allows reflected Cross-Site Scripting (e.g. q=</script><script>alert(1)</script> or q='-alert(1)-').

SearchHandler explicitly disables the browser's XSS Auditor by setting the 'X-XSS-Protection' header to '0'. Combined with the reflected, unescaped output of the 'q' parameter, this removes a defense-in-depth control and facilitates reflected XSS attacks.

UploadHandler derives the file extension from the user-supplied filename (file1['filename']) via os.path.splitext and concatenates it into the output path '/tmp/' + final_filename without sanitization. A crafted extension containing path traversal sequences (e.g. '.../../etc/cron.d/x') can cause the uploaded content to be written to attacker-chosen locations. There is also no validation of file type/content.

The UploadHandler (POST /upload), ContentHandler (GET /read) and ServerHandler (POST /server.html) perform sensitive actions (file write, arbitrary file read, command execution) without any authentication or authorization checks. Any unauthenticated remote user can invoke these handlers.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: The Tornado application is configured with 'debug': True. In debug mode Tornado serves detailed tracebacks and stack traces to clients on errors, which can leak source code, file paths, and other sensitive internal information. Debug mode should be disabled in production.

Hardcoded user credentials (including 'admin'/'admin') are embedded in the source code and stored in plaintext in the database. Passwords are not hashed, and the default admin/admin credential is trivially guessable. This exposes account credentials in source control.

The login POST handler prints the full raw request body (which contains the submitted username and plaintext password) to the server log/console. This exposes sensitive credentials in logs (CWE-532). The same pattern of logging request bodies appears in ServerHandler.post (line 123).

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File
